title: Bill-of-record for speculative prefix warmups and multiplexed microbatches
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Background: We observed large month-over-month variance in billed token counts for customers using prefix warmups and aggressive prefetching. Traffic patterns that multiplex many small microbatches onto the same GPU combined with speculative prefix warmups lead to ambiguous token provenance: which logical request should be charged for tokens served from KV cache or created by speculative prefetch?

Goal: Define a single, auditable bill-of-record for all tokenized work performed across the runtime that covers: (1) speculative prefix warmups, (2) KV cache hits/partial hits, and (3) multiplexed/coalesced microbatches. The solution must be backwards-compatible for hosted billing, produce audit logs for Dedicated/Private customers, and keep latency and throughput regressions < 3%.

High-level approach: Introduce token provenance tags on metered rows (request_owner, microbatch_id, provenance=[compute|cached|prefetch]) and a deterministic attribution rule-set: - Prefetch tokens created by speculative warmups are attributed to the initiator customer until a TTL or sharing policy reassigns cost. - KV cache hits do not bill compute tokens but do bill a small "cache-serve" token unit to the microbatch that requested the cached prefix unless the cache entry was created by an earlier warmup that has remaining billable balance. - When microbatches are coalesced on the GPU, charge compute tokens proportionally by owner-requested sequence length and charge cached tokens to request owners that caused the original cache fills.

This ticket scopes the RFC, implementable metering changes (metering-service + runtime headers), and a canary plan with dashboards and customer-facing billing FAQ language.
acceptance_criteria: Define the deterministic attribution rules in an RFC and get PM + Finance approval
Add provenance fields to metering event schema and wire through runtime and metering-service
Implement a billing export that reconciles cached vs compute tokens per customer for the last 30 days and validate against existing invoices with <0.5% variance in control group
Canary rollout to 5% of hosted traffic with live dashboards showing cost deltas, error rates, and latency impact
Docs/FAQ for enterprise customers and an opt-out knob for sharing prefetch costs
tasks: Add provenance header to front-end router and downstream runtime (X-Token-Provenance) - owner: Marco
Extend metering-service schema: add fields request_owner, microbatch_id, provenance - owner: billing-eng
Billing export script to compute per-customer cached vs compute split (backfill last 90d) - owner: finance-eng
Canary dashboard: cost-delta, per-customer invoice diff, latency tail (p99), and batch-coalescing ratio - owner: observability
Customer-facing FAQ and opt-out flow for Dedicated/Private - owner: PM
comments: 2026-03-10 Asha: Opened ticket after postmortem SIG on March billing spike. Attached preliminary spreadsheet comparing cached_vs_compute across top 50 customers.
2026-03-11 Marco: Prototyped adding X-Token-Provenance header in runtime; small overhead (~0.2ms/request). Raising concern: adding provenance on every token event increases metering volume ~12%.

2026-03-11 Finance (Elena): Prefer attribution that minimizes invoice churn. Proposal: bill prefetch to owner until a share threshold (e.g., when >60% of subsequent hits across other customers reference same cache entry then start pro-rata sharing). Need business approval.
2026-03-12 Design review (Sam): Suggested clear customer UX in Console: show 'Prefetch billed by' and a time-series of prefetch-created entries and how costs shift when sharing threshold crossed.

2026-03-12 Marco: Edge case note — partial KV hits where first N tokens are cached and remainder computed. Decided to attribute cached tokens to cache owner and computed tokens to request owner for that call. Implementation requires per-token provenance at emit time; we will coarse-grain by contiguous cached spans to reduce event volume.

2026-03-13 Observability (Priya): Created dashboard draft: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/redwood/billing-playbook?orgId=1; initial canary metrics show a +0.9% billed tokens for prefetch owners in small internal test cluster.
2026-03-13 Marco: Opened PR to runtime to add header and propagate microbatch_id: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4392
2026-03-13 Security (Riley): No direct secrets changes. Flagging that Dedicated customers will want KMS audit bindings for billing exports — follow-up ticket TBD.
